explanations.answer: The knowledge of God and of Jesus

explanations.answer: The strength of their own effort

explanations.answer: So they can share in God's own nature

explanations.answer: So they can stay free from hard times

That one's easy to grab, friend, because we all like the idea.

explanations.answer: On top of the one before it

explanations.answer: In place of the one before it
explanations.explanation: Peter says to add “to” each quality, not to trade one for another. Nobody swaps virtue out for knowledge. It's like adding chocolate chips to the dough, because you don't take the dough out first. The list stacks.

explanations.answer: Off to the side by itself
explanations.explanation: Every quality in Peter's list is added to the one before it. He writes “and to knowledge, self-control,” so each one is linked to the last. They're not scattered around. A pile of toppings next to the cookie is not a cookie, friend.

Peter says that if you have these qualities and keep growing in them, “they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” That's just what he writes. Ineffective and unproductive, friend. Those are the two things he says it keeps you from.

explanations.answer: That he was cleansed from his past sins

explanations.answer: That he still has work to finish
